title: Fleet Placement Arbitrator and Residency Boundary Guard
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a Fleet Placement Arbitrator (FPA) service that centralizes placement decisions for regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets. The FPA enforces throughput guarantees, autoscaling policies, and data residency constraints while providing safe failover behavior and decommitment controls for Dedicated customers.

Goals:
- Single decision point for placement policies that can be audited and simulated.
- Ensure throughput guarantees (committed qps/tokens) are honored across zones with graceful degradation when capacity is constrained.
- Support policy primitives: zone affinity, hard residency locks, soft residency preferences, preemption windows, and decommit safety windows.
- Autoscaling integration: provide scale-up/scale-down guidance and vetoes based on latency SLOs and throughput contracts.
- Failover semantics: orchestrated cross-zone spillover with prioritized routing lanes and fast rollback.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement UI console features (Console integration ticket will follow).
- Does not change billing model; cost reporting handled by Optimize pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
- FPA prototype accepts placement requests and returns a deterministic placement decision for region+zone with reason code.
- Throughput guarantee test: with simulated committed load, FPA prevents placement that would overcommit a zone's reserved throughput.
- Autoscale veto: under sustained high-latency feedback, FPA can prevent scale-down for pools with active throughput contracts.
- Residency guard: placement decisions must include a residency tag; placements that would violate a hard residency constraint are rejected.
- Failover plan: when a zone is marked degraded, FPA re-routes new allocations using spillover policy and records metrics for routed fraction.
- Integration tests complete in CI with deterministic seed and pass in the dedicated-sim job.
design_notes:
High-level design:
- FPA is an idempotent, versioned policy engine that evaluates a placement request against: pool contract (committed throughput), zone capacity snapshot, residency constraints, autoscale state, and active failover flags.
- Policy ordering: hard residency > committed throughput > latency risk > soft preferences.
- Decision outputs: chosen region, chosen zone(s), placement type (primary, spillover), reason code, advisory actions (start-prewarm, pin-kv-cache), and decision TTL.
- State model: read-only capacity view from Fleet Registry + short-lived leases for temporary allocations. Leases have decommit timers to prevent rapid oscillation.
- Safe-drain mechanism: when evicting allocations to drain a zone, FPA issues staged relocation windows and honors decommit safety window configured per commitment tier.

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralized vs decentralized: centralized simplifies policy and auditing but introduces a control-plane dependency. Mitigation: FPA will run in high-availability clusters with cached policy copies and local fallback logic in agents.
- Strict residency enforcement can reduce capacity utilization. We add soft-preference mode to allow controlled spillover under operator-approved exceptions.
api_contract:
POST /v1/fpa/decide
Request fields: pool_id, requested_tokens, latency_slo_ms, residency_hint, candidate_regions (optional), request_id, client_tier
Response fields: decision_id, region, zone, placement_mode, reason_code, advisory_actions, ttl_seconds, decision_version
Error codes: 409 (residency_violation), 503 (insufficient_capacity), 422 (invalid_request)
Notes: Decisions are signed with a decision_version to allow downstream components to verify compatibility.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy FPA in us-west1 as read-only advisory (no enforcement) for 2 weeks; collect decision parity metrics.
- Phase 2 (soft-enforce): enforce placement for low-risk pools and non-customer-impacting allocations; run chaos tests on orchestrator to simulate zone degradation.
- Phase 3 (full-enforce): enforce for all Dedicated pools with canary rollouts by customer commit tier; provide kill-switch per account.
- Post-rollout: enable continuous monitoring with a dashboard for decision rejections and a weekly audit report for residency violations.
- Rollback: revert enforcement config to advisory mode and drain FPA control plane if we observe >0.5% client errors attributable to the FPA in 1 hour.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation with exhaustive permutations of residency and throughput constraints.
- Load test: synthetic allocation flood to measure FPA latency and rate limits; target p95 < 120ms at 1000 rps.
- Integration: CI job 'dedicated-sim' will run end-to-end placement scenarios including zone failure, preemption windows, and decommit windows.
- Chaos test: orchestrator + FPA under simulated region outage; verify safe-drain windows and correctness of spillover decisions.
- Security: pen test on FPA admin endpoints and review of signed decision tokens.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: defined primary policy primitives and scoped prototype. Action: Marco to spin up policy proto in test cluster.

2026-03-03 - Marco Nguyen: Prototype v0 ready. Returns deterministic decisions based on capacity snapshot. Observed race when two concurrent requests allocate remaining tokens — added short lease and CAS on registry write as mitigation.
2026-03-05 - Lena Ortiz (Infra): Suggested HA architecture: two active FPA clusters per region with local policy cache and eventual sync. Also recommends exposing metrics via runtime exporter.

2026-03-07 - Marco Nguyen: Implemented residency rejection with explicit error code (409). Wrote unit tests for hard vs soft residency modes.
Open: need product guidance on default behavior for soft residency spillovers.

2026-03-09 - Product (Jorge Silva): We decide default: soft residency allowed for lower commitment tiers, hard residency for enterprise tiers. PM to update SLA docs and expose flag in Dedicated pool config.
2026-03-10 - Marco Nguyen: Began wiring autoscaler hook (scale-veto API). Next: integration tests with autoscaler and adjust p95 latency target.
